NODE: bpN:p0:integrable#IsAnalyticIntegrable
KIND: definition
TITLE: Analytic integrable part, $h\in A_s(D)$: KAM.Nekhoroshev.IsAnalyticIntegrable
STATEMENT_SOURCE: blueprint-N/parts/p0-conventions.tex#bpN:p0:integrable@L106-L119
PROOF_SOURCE: -
CONTRACT_ID: nekhoroshev.IsAnalyticIntegrable
CONTRACT_VERSION: 1
SOURCE_HYPOTHESES: h : ℂⁿ → ℂ; R, s ∈ ℝ
SOURCE_QUANTIFIERS: n; R, s; h
SOURCE_CONCLUSION: IsAnalyticIntegrable R s h holds iff (i) h complex differentiable on B(0,R)_s; (ii) h continuous on the closure of B(0,R)_s in ℂⁿ; (iii) ∃ A ≥ 0 with ¦h(I)¦ ≤ A on B(0,R)_s; (iv) Im h(I) = 0 for all I ∈ 𝓑_s(R); (v) h_ℝ is C³ on 𝓑_s(R) (real Fréchet sense). No numerical bound on h is fixed
CONSTANT_SCOPE: A is existentially quantified inside clause (iii); this definition fixes no numerical bound on h. Independence of the headline constants from A is a separate theorem-level requirement.

NODE: bpN:p0:pert#IsAnalyticPerturbation
KIND: definition
TITLE: Analytic perturbation of size $\varepsilon$: KAM.Nekhoroshev.IsAnalyticPerturbation
STATEMENT_SOURCE: blueprint-N/parts/p0-conventions.tex#bpN:p0:pert@L121-L133
PROOF_SOURCE: -
CONTRACT_ID: nekhoroshev.IsAnalyticPerturbation
CONTRACT_VERSION: 1
SOURCE_HYPOTHESES: f : ℂⁿ × ℂⁿ → ℂ; R, s, ε ∈ ℝ
SOURCE_QUANTIFIERS: n; R, s, ε; f
SOURCE_CONCLUSION: IsAnalyticPerturbation R s ε f holds iff ε ≥ 0 and (i) f complex differentiable on D_s(R) and continuous on its closure; (ii) f(θ+k,I) = f(θ,I) for (θ,I) ∈ D_s(R), k ∈ ℤⁿ; (iii) Im f(θ,I) = 0 for θ ∈ ℝⁿ, I ∈ 𝓑_s(R); (iv) ¦f(z)¦ ≤ ε on D_s(R). (Size is ≤ ε, not the source strict bound.) For ε = 0 it forces f = 0 on D_s(R)

NODE: bpN:p0:head
KIND: theorem
TITLE: N-HEAD-C: exponential stability, complex Hessian bound
STATEMENT_SOURCE: blueprint-N/parts/p0-conventions.tex#bpN:p0:head@L204-L237
PROOF_SOURCE: blueprint-N/parts/p10-assembly.tex#bpN:p10:head@L143-L155
CONTRACT_ID: nekhoroshev.quasiConvex_nekhoroshev_complexBound
CONTRACT_VERSION: 1
SOURCE_HYPOTHESES: a Lean frozen statement; n ≥ 3, R, s, M, m, M_ℂ, ω_min > 0 (outer); for h, f, ε: (H1) IsAnalyticIntegrable R s h; (H2) HasComplexHessianBound R s h M_ℂ; (H3) ω_min ≤ ¦ω_h(I)¦ for every I ∈ B(0,R) (max norm); (H4) IsStrictlyQuasiConvex 𝓑_s(R) h m; (H5) HasDerivativeBounds 𝓑_s(R) h M; (H6) IsAnalyticPerturbation R s ε f; (H7) 0 < ε ≤ ε₀; θ₀ ∈ ℝⁿ, I₀ ∈ B(0,R/2); τ := T exp(c ε^{−1/(2n)}), H = H_{h,f}
SOURCE_QUANTIFIERS: n ≥ 3; R, s, M, m, M_ℂ, ω_min > 0; then ∃ C, T, c, ε₀ > 0 with C ε₀^{1/(2n)} ≤ R/4; then ∀ h : ℂⁿ → ℂ, f : ℂⁿ × ℂⁿ → ℂ, ε ∈ ℝ (with H1–H7); then ∀ θ₀ ∈ ℝⁿ, I₀ ∈ B(0,R/2); then ∃ z : ℝ → ℝⁿ × ℝⁿ
SOURCE_CONCLUSION: (a) z(0) = (θ₀,I₀); (b) IsSolutionOn H B(0,R) [−τ,τ] z; (c) ¦z(t)_2 − I₀¦ ≤ C ε^{1/(2n)} for all ¦t¦ ≤ τ; (d) uniqueness: for every L ∈ [0,τ] and y with y(0) = (θ₀,I₀) and IsSolutionOn H B(0,R) [−L,L] y: y(t) = z(t) for t ∈ [−L,L]
CONSTANT_SCOPE: C, T, c, ε₀ depend only on (n, R, s, M, m, M_ℂ, ω_min), chosen before h, f, ε, θ₀, I₀; no dependence on the bound A of IsAnalyticIntegrable(iii); z may depend on all data

NODE: bpN:p0:partial
KIND: theorem
TITLE: N-PARTIAL-CONVEX: exponential stability of the fast actions, definite fast part, slow--fast
STATEMENT_SOURCE: blueprint-N/parts/p0-conventions.tex#bpN:p0:partial@L319-L335
PROOF_SOURCE: blueprint-N/parts/p11c-partial-stability.tex#bpN:p0:partial@L170-L180
CONTRACT_ID: nekhoroshev.d25.partialConvex_nekhoroshev
CONTRACT_VERSION: 1
SOURCE_HYPOTHESES: a Lean frozen statement; n ≥ 2, k ≥ 1, G, G' ⊂ ℝⁿ open and convex, D ⊂ Ph_k open, ρ, g, m, M_ℂ ∈ ℝ with ρ > 0, M_ℂ > 0, B̄(I,ρ) ⊂ G' for every I ∈ G (closed max-norm ball); h : ℂⁿ → ℂ complex differentiable and complex C² on G'_ρ, Im h(I) = 0 for real I ∈ G'_ρ, ‖D²h(z)‖ ≤ M_ℂ on G'_ρ, HasDefiniteFastPart G' ρ g m h; then for μ ∈ (0,μ₀), P with IsPartialPerturbation G' D ρ P, C > 0, z : ℝ → Ph_{n+k}: (Z1) IsSolutionOn H_μ {𝖨 : fast(𝖨) ∈ G} [0,C] z with H_μ = Re h(fast 𝖨) + μ Re P(cx(φ,𝖨)) (degenerateHamiltonian (realPart h) (Re P ∘ cx) μ); (Z2) fast(z(0)_2) ∈ core(G, μ^{b_n}); t ∈ [0, min(C, μ^{−1} exp(μ^{−a_n}))] with (slow z(u)_1, slow z(u)_2) ∈ core(D, μ^{b_n}) for all u ∈ [0,t]
SOURCE_QUANTIFIERS: n, k; G, G', D, ρ, g, m, M_ℂ, h (with their hypotheses); then ∃ μ₀ > 0; then ∀ μ ∈ (0,μ₀), P, C > 0, z (with Z1, Z2); then ∀ t ∈ [0, min(C, μ^{−1} exp(μ^{−a_n}))] with slow confinement on [0,t]
SOURCE_CONCLUSION: ¦fast(z(t)_2) − fast(z(0)_2)¦ ≤ ½ μ^{b_n}
CONSTANT_SCOPE: μ₀ > 0 depends only on (n, k, G, G', D, ρ, g, m, M_ℂ, h) and is chosen before μ, P, C, z, t; a_n = 2/(6n² − 3n + 14), b_n = 3/(6n² − 3n + 14); slow confinement is tested only on [0,t]; the initial erosion core(G, μ^{b_n}) is used only as fast(z(0)_2) ∈ G

FROZEN_DECL: KAM.Nekhoroshev.partialConvex_nekhoroshev

PROOF_SOURCE: -
CONTRACT_ID: bpN:p1:constants#data
CONTRACT_VERSION: 1
SOURCE_HYPOTHESES: n ≥ 3 (only n ≥ 2 used by Pöschel); R, s, M, m, M_ℂ, ω_min > 0
SOURCE_QUANTIFIERS: n≥3; R,s,M,m,M_ℂ,ω_min>0; then successive definitions in the displayed order
SOURCE_CONCLUSION: Defines a = 1/(2n); q = m/n, B_c = nM_ℂ+q, μ = q/2, ℓ = ω_min q/(8(B_c+q)), r₀ = min(s/2, R/8, ℓ/(2B_c), 4ω_min/μ), A = 11B_c/μ, s₀ = πs, σ = πs/4, F = 2π coth^n(πs/4), ε_* = 2πμ r₀²/(2^{10}A^{2n}), C = (r₀/A)(F/ε_*)^a, c = (s₀/(6√n))(ε_*/F)^a, T = A²s₀/(4πnM), ε₀ = min(ε_*/F, (R/(4C))^{2n}); Pöschel data m_P = 2πμ, ℓ_P = 2πℓ, M_P = 2πB_c, A_P = 11M_P/m_P = A, ε_{0,P} = m_P r₀²/(2^{10}A_P^{2n}) = ε_*, R₀ = r₀/A, P = {J ∈ ℝⁿ : ¦J¦ ≤ R/2}
CONSTANT_SCOPE: Every defined constant depends only on (n,R,s,M,m,M_ℂ,ω_min), before h,f,ε,θ₀,I₀. The dictionary A is distinct from the existential bound in IsAnalyticIntegrable.

NODE: bpN:p6:iterative
KIND: theorem
TITLE: Iterative Lemma
STATEMENT_SOURCE: blueprint-N/parts/p6-normal-form.tex#bpN:p6:iterative@L93-L108
PROOF_SOURCE: blueprint-N/parts/p6-normal-form.tex#bpN:p6:iterative@L109-L127
CONTRACT_ID: bpN:p6:iterative
CONTRACT_VERSION: 1
SOURCE_HYPOTHESES: (N1), (N2), KLr<=alpha/p (p>1, q=p/(p-1)); s>0; rho,sigma>0 with 2rho<r, 2sigma<s; abar=2πalpha; H=h+g+f on D_{r,s}, g=sum_{j in J} g_j as in the setting (any finite decomposition), f in O(r,s); delta=|f|_{r,s}<=abar rho sigma/(4q) (equivalently u=q delta/(abar rho sigma)<=1/4)
SOURCE_QUANTIFIERS: (D,r,K,alpha,L,Lambda,h); p; s; rho; sigma; g, J, g_j; f
SOURCE_CONCLUSION: there is phi in O(r,s) (that of the homological equation, |phi|_{r,s}<=q delta/abar) such that Phi=X^1_phi satisfies (a) Phi holomorphic on D_{r-3rho/2,s-3sigma/2} into D_{r-rho,s-sigma}, canonical (DPhi^T J DPhi=J), Phi(theta+k,I)=Phi(theta,I)+(k,0), injective on D_{r-2rho,s-2sigma} with left inverse X^{-1}_phi; (b) nu_{rho,sigma}(Phi-id)<=u, |Phi_theta-theta|_inf<=q delta/(abar rho), |Phi_I-I|_inf<=q delta/(e abar sigma), |DPhi-1|_nu<=2u on D_{r-2rho,s-2sigma}; (c) H∘Phi=h+g_++f_+ on D_{r-2rho,s-2sigma}, g_+=g+P_Lambda T_K f, |g_+-g|_{r,s}<=delta, f_+ in O(r-2rho,s-2sigma); (d) |f_+|_{r-2rho,s-2sigma}<=(1-2q delta/(abar rho sigma))^{-1}(2q/(e abar rho sigma)(|g|_*+delta)+e^{-2πK sigma})delta; (e) if Lambda=-Lambda and h,g,f real on real points then phi, g_+, f_+ real on real points and Phi maps real points to real points
CONSTANT_SCOPE: all constants explicit; depend only on (n,r,s,rho,sigma,K,alpha,L,p) and on delta, |g|_*; no dependence on f or H beyond delta and |g|_*

SOURCE_CONCLUSION: (a) for a K-lattice Lambda, Lambda in M_K iff E_K intersect W_Lambda is contained in Lambda; Theta is maximal, and a saturated K-lattice is maximal; (b) every K-lattice Gamma is contained in a maximal K-lattice of equal dimension, including the rank-one assertion for nonzero k in E_K; (c) IF Lambda in M_K and k in E_K minus Lambda, then k not in W_Lambda, dim Lambda < n, and Lambda+Zk is a K-lattice of dimension dim Lambda+1; (d) IF Lambda in M_K and dim Lambda=n then E_K is contained in Lambda; if also K>=1 then Lambda=Z^n; Z^n in M_K for K>=1; if 0<=K<1 then M_K={Theta}; (e) IF Lambda in M_K has dimension d then 1<=|Lambda|<=K^d

TITLE: [K] (E11) Lebesgue measure on products and boxes
STATEMENT_SOURCE: blueprint/parts/p1-analysis.tex#bp:p1:ext-measure@L100-L109
PROOF_SOURCE: -
CONTRACT_ID: K:bp:p1:ext-measure
CONTRACT_VERSION: 1
SOURCE_HYPOTHESES: finite dimensions d1, d2 >= 0; A, B, E measurable; E_1 subset E_2 subset ... measurable; a box prod_i [a_i,b_i]
SOURCE_QUANTIFIERS: for all measurable A, B, E and increasing measurable sequences E_j, and all boxes
SOURCE_CONCLUSION: Lebesgue measure on R^{d1} x R^{d2} = R^{d1+d2} is the product measure: meas(A x B) = meas A meas B and meas E = int meas(E_x) dx (Tonelli); meas(union E_j) = lim meas E_j; closed and open boxes with the same corners have measure prod (b_i - a_i), so box boundaries are null
